title: fix(sdk-recorder): release capture after encoder failures
body:
When a browser encoder raises `MediaRecorder.error`, the SDK stays in its recording/paused phase, retains the camera and microphone, and keeps its timers alive. If the failure happens while stopping, it can also upload the failed encoder's partial output.

Handle errors only for the current encoder, release capture and timers before notifying listeners, and transition to `error` once. Resolve the stop gate with the original error so a pending `stop()` rejects without uploading or creating an unhandled rejection. Late events from a destroyed/replaced encoder cannot affect the replacement. The listener-registration cast is reused for unsubscribe to fix the existing strict-TypeScript error while validating this source; this supporting change is identical to #3380/#3387.

Validation: all 41 SDK tests pass. Six new cases cover active/paused failures, timer cleanup, missing native error details, failure during stop, a late old-encoder error, and replacement from an error handler; five fail before the fix. Full SDK strict typecheck and ESM/declaration build, strict new-test typecheck, scoped Biome and diff checks pass.

Reproduce: `bun test packages/sdk-recorder`, then `cd packages/sdk-recorder && bun run typecheck && bun run build`.

This handles capture-time encoding errors; #3380 handles asynchronous upload ownership. Their combined 49-test suite and package typecheck also pass locally after combining their overlapping stop-gate changes. Browser media devices/events are controlled in tests; physical capture and codec failures were not exercised. No dependencies or public signatures change.
author: vedanth-jadhav
